newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power steady in thin activity.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power steady in thin activity.

text.p: Day-head prices in the U.S. Northeast bulk electricity market Tuesday held steady against Monday levels in thin, pre-holiday activity.

Some northern areas of the region would plunge into a deep freeze New Year's Day with night temperatures as much as 20 degrees Fahrenheit below zero. Wednesday readings in other parts of the Northeast will likely range in the teens to 40s.
Extended forecasts showed a warming trend would moderate temperatures near normal toward the end of the week.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices for Thursday delivery in the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) stayed in a $23.00-$24.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) range.
Off-peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in western NYPP held in a notional range of $14.00-$15.00.
In eastern NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Thursday was steady at $26.50-$28.00/MWh.
Eastern NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Thursday stayed at $18.00-$19.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border remained in $30.00-$33.00 range.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for day-ahead delivery to the NU border was still pegged at $20.00-$22.00.
Swing prices of delivery to the New York City gate were pegged today $3.60-$3.80 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) range, up from Monday's $3.40-$3.50.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub natgas futures ended up 7.3 cents/mmBtu at $2.750.
